## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The macro backdrop in May 2026 is defined by an uncomfortable stagflationary dynamic: elevated oil prices driven by the US-Iran war are simultaneously lifting headline inflation and suppressing global growth. US CPI YoY stands at 3.95% as of April, well above the Fed's 2% target, while the effective Fed Funds rate is 3.64% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS]. The 10-year Treasury yield has risen to 4.57% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10], reflecting a hawkish repricing after April FOMC minutes showed a majority of Fed officials are open to rate hikes if inflation remains persistent. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson explicitly stated that policy is "mildly restrictive" and called it "healthy" that markets were pricing rate hike scenarios [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-20/feds-paulson-says-current-policy-appropriate-healthy-consider-extended].

The transition to a Warsh-led Fed under the Trump administration has amplified this hawkish pivot. FOMC minutes from April showed that a majority of participants flagged "policy firming" as likely appropriate if inflation persists, with "some" participants warning about de-anchoring inflation expectations from sustained energy price pressures and tariff effects [Source: https://www.axios.com/2026/05/20/fed-rates-minutes-warsh]. The 2-year Treasury yield at 4.04% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2] continues to price a curve that reflects near-term policy hold with rising tail risk of hikes. PPI MoM is running at 2.66% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PPIACO], adding pipeline inflation pressure.

Equities have proven remarkably resilient in 2026, with the S&P 500 at 7,445.72 [Source: Yahoo Finance (^GSPC)] and Dow at 50,285.66 [Source: Yahoo Finance (^DJI)] near record highs. Barclays noted year-to-date inflows to US equity funds of $180 billion, more than double the five-year median, as foreign demand for US equities accelerates [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/market-correction-equities-stocks-bonds-iran-inflation.html]. VIX at 16.7 [Source: Yahoo Finance (^VIX)] reflects relatively contained near-term fear despite the complex geopolitical environment. Nvidia earnings, Walmart results, and the Lowe's/Target earnings beat — with Lowe's Q1 comparable sales +0.6% and Target comparable sales +5.6% [Source: https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/05/target-corporation-reports-first-quarter-earnings] — have supported the consumer-resilience narrative.

The Bank of Japan is signalling approaching rate hikes, with BoJ board member Junko Koeda stating it is "reasonable" to raise rates to address high inflation driven by Middle East tensions [Source: https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/bank-of-japan-policymaker-signals-that-rate-hike-might-be-approaching-6a90860b]. Bank Indonesia delivered a surprise 50bps hike to 5.25% [Source: https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/bank-indonesia-delivers-first-rate-hike-in-years-as-rupiah-flounders-risks-rise-af2c5047], the first in years, as EM central banks tighten defensively. The global tightening impulse is broadening beyond the Fed, creating a challenging environment for risk assets particularly sensitive to rate differentials.

- Global bond yields have surged approximately 70bps since the war began, and the UN lowered its 2026 global GDP growth forecast to 2.5% from 2.7%, warning of a potential decline to 2.1% in an adverse scenario [Source: https://www.greenwichtime.com/news/world/article/un-lowers-forecast-for-global-economic-growth-in-22267375.php].

2. **Fed Speaker Slate** (Week of May 25) — Multiple FOMC participants speaking in the wake of the hawkish April minutes; any escalation in rate-hike language will drive Treasury yields, USD, and risk assets.

3. **Bank of Japan Policy Signals** (Week of May 25) — BoJ board hawkishness is building toward a potential June/July rate decision; USD/JPY and Nikkei are the primary vehicles.

4. **US PCE Deflator** (Expected ~May 30) — The Fed's preferred inflation measure will be critical in calibrating the rate-hike probability; a hot print would accelerate the repricing.

5. **Strait of Hormuz Shipping Data** (Ongoing, daily) — Supertanker movements through Hormuz are the real-time barometer of the energy supply disruption; any escalation or normalisation drives immediate oil price moves with second-order effects across all asset classes.
